Corporate Appropriation.text:
CORPORATE APPROPRIATION

LOBO'S TOP 40  /  MAP #1  /  300 POINTS  /  ITS 18

Scoring and game length

MAIN OBJECTIVES - SCORE AT GAME END

2 OP - Finish with the enemy Prototype captured.

+1 OP - That captured Prototype is also in your deployment zone.

1 OP - Your Prototype is still intact and the enemy has not captured it.

3 OP - Your own Prototype has been destroyed.

1 OP - You obtained more weapons / equipment from Panoplies than your opponent.

CLASSIFIED OBJECTIVES AND ENDING

Each player has 3 Classified Objectives, worth 1 OP apiece.

Maximum score: 10 OP. The intact-Prototype point and the destroyed-Prototype points are mutually exclusive.

The game normally ends after Game Round 3.

If a player begins an Active Turn in Retreat!, play ends when that Active Turn finishes.

Setup and deployment

300-POINT MAP SETUP

Play area: 48 x 48 inches. Army allowance: 300 points / 6 SWC.

Deploy from the opposite X edges. Each deployment zone is 12 inches deep: X=-24 to -12, or X=+12 to +24.

The two thin colored lines show only the forward deployment boundaries.

The yellow dashed lines enclose the central exclusion zone, from X=-4 to X=+4. Airborne Deployment and Superior Deployment skills cannot deploy inside that band.

OBJECTIVES AND SPECIALISTS

Two Prototypes, one owned by each player. Before deployment, the player taking the second turn assigns ownership.

Prototype positions: (X=0, Z=-12) and (X=0, Z=+12). Two Panoplies: (X=-12, Z=0) and (X=+12, Z=0). Use 40 mm objective tokens / scenery.

Scenario Specialists: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Chain of Command and Specialist Operative.

Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Servant Peripherals for tasks restricted to Specialists. Picking up a Prototype and using a Panoply do not require a Specialist.

Prototype profile, attacks and defenses

PROFILE AND DESTRUCTION

ARM 6 | BTS 6 | STR 3 | Silhouette 3. Other listed Attributes are absent. Fixed CC Roll: 8. GizmoKit PH: 9.

Only anti-materiel close-combat attacks or placed D-Charges can damage a Prototype.

A Prototype is destroyed at 3 Wounds; remove it from the table.

Engineer and GizmoKit can target a Prototype.

During Game Round 1, attacks against Prototypes are forbidden. The Pick Up Prototype scenario skill is the exception.

AUTOMATED DEFENSE SYSTEM

A CC attack against a Prototype triggers its ADS reaction and becomes a Face to Face Roll.

The ADS uses a fixed result of 8. No modifiers may change the attacking trooper's CC Attribute for this attack.

If the ADS result succeeds, the attacker takes a Stun hit: make one BTS Saving Roll against PS 5.

Immunity (Enhanced) and Immunity (BTS) do not protect against that ADS hit.

The ADS responds to CC attacks. Picking up a Prototype uses its own scenario skill.

Picking up, carrying and capturing

PICK UP PROTOTYPE

Short Skill with Attack and Scenario labels. No roll is needed; any trooper can perform it when the requirements are met.

Be in Silhouette contact with an unattended enemy Prototype, or with an allied trooper in Normal State who is carrying the enemy Prototype.

Only a Model can carry a Prototype. Marker states, including Camouflage, Impersonation and Holoechoes, cannot carry one.

Keep the Prototype token on the table, in Silhouette contact with its carrier.

MOVEMENT, DROPPING AND CAPTURE

A carrier cannot declare Move as the second Basic Short Skill of an Order. Baggage provides an exception.

A carrier that enters, or is already in, a Null State drops the Prototype. Place it slightly outside contact with that trooper.

Prototype tokens do not obstruct movement or Line of Fire.

At game end, an enemy Prototype counts as captured only while carried by your non-Null Model, which must not be in Silhouette contact with a non-Null enemy Model.

Using Panoplies

USE PANOPLIES

Short Skill with Attack and Scenario labels. The trooper must be in Silhouette contact with the Panoply.

On a successful WIP Roll, choose either D-Charges or a roll on the Panoply Chart to receive a weapon or item.

After succeeding, that trooper cannot use the same Panoply again. The other Panoply remains available.

Booty, or another skill that explicitly permits it, removes the WIP Roll requirement.

ITEMS AND RELOADING

If a Panoply Chart result grants a weapon or item the trooper already has, the chart roll may be repeated.

A trooper in contact can spend one Short Skill to cancel its Unloaded State.

Track acquired weapons and equipment for both players. The player with the higher total at game end scores 1 OP; a tie scores neither player.

The next tab contains the full d20 Panoply Chart, including the separate TAG results.

Panoply Chart - roll a d20

ROLLS 1-12

1-2     ARM +1

3-4     Light Flamethrower

5-6     Grenades

7-8     DA CC Weapon

9        Multispectral Visor L1

10      EXP CC Weapon

11      Adhesive Launcher Rifle

12      TAG: Immunity (AP)
           Other troop types: ARM +2

ROLLS 13-20

13      Panzerfaust

14      Monofilament CC Weapon

15      MOV 8-4

16      TAG: BS Attack (Shock)
           Other troop types: MULTI Rifle

17      MULTI Sniper Rifle

18      TAG: Immunity (ARM)
           Other troop types: ARM +4

19      Mimetism (-6)

20      TAG: BS Attack (+1B)
           Other troop types: HMG

ITS 18, version 2026.09.11, pp. 53-58. Each player selects tabs independently.

Crossing Lines.text:
CROSSING LINES  -  VEYRA GATE

Crossing Lines | 48 x 48 inches | ITS18, September 24 revision

Each player has a 12-inch rear zone and a 4-inch forward strip on the opposing half. Up to 75 Army Points may start in that strip. The two bands between deployment zones are both Dead Zones and Exclusion Zones.

Score 1 OP per Dead Zone dominated at the end of each round. At game end, score 2 OP if you dominate both and 1 OP per antenna you control. Specialists activate in Silhouette contact with a Normal WIP Roll. No deployment in contact with antennas.

Baggage adds 20 Victory Points for zone domination. No HVT or Classified Deck. Use the official packet for the full rules. The +4 and +8 lines are optional references.

Double Bind.text:
DOUBLE BIND / NEON SHOGUNATE

ITS18 / 300 points / Lobo Top 40 Final / 48 x 48 inches

Neon Shogunate / Lobo Top 40 Final

THE FINAL

The manor and Lantern Market frame a clash over three city communications nodes. Garage, bathhouse, shrine, transit stop and greenhouse give each approach a different character. This version uses Lobo's edited Living City save and keeps the placed consoles and rearranged scenery.

CHOOSE YOUR OPERATION

When choosing Deployment, that player immediately selects Encryption, Sabotage or Secure Vector. The opponent then selects one of the two remaining operations. Players therefore pursue different main objectives. Each player also scores the shared secondary and their Classified.

Board, objectives and deployment

SETUP

300 points / 6 SWC on a 48 x 48 inch board. Opposing edges are X=-24 and X=+24; 12-inch deployment fronts X=-12 and X=+12. Exclusion Zone: the central 8-inch strip, X=-4 to +4. Skills with Airborne Deployment or Superior Deployment labels cannot deploy inside it. DZ +4/+8 buttons are skill guides only.

THREE ANTENNAS

Three console Antennas have 40 mm bases and 32 mm visual heights, checked from their Unity mesh and transform hierarchy. Base centers are X=0 at Z=-12, 0 and +12. The official current downloadable mission text omits its placement diagram: these centers implement the approved three-node layout and still need an event-diagram cross-check. Each Zone of Influence is a 120 mm Circular Template centered on its Antenna. Guides remain after a model is destroyed.

Three distinct main objectives

ENCRYPTION / SABOTAGE

Encryption, at each Game Round end: 1 OP if you have at least one Activated Antenna; +1 OP if you have at least two. Sabotage, at game end: 2 OP per Antenna you destroyed. Only Sabotage players may attack Antennas as objectives. Only one Antenna may be destroyed per turn; after one is destroyed, damage to another that turn has no effect.

SECURE VECTOR / SHARED

Secure Vector, at each Game Round end: 1 OP for dominating at least one Zone of Influence; +1 OP for dominating two or more. Dominate by having more qualifying Victory Points in the zone; more than half a trooper's base must be inside. Non-Null Baggage adds 20 VP; Shasvastii can count while Unconscious. Shared: 2 OP for killing more Army Points than your opponent. Each player has one Classified worth 2 OP. Total maximum: 10 OP.

Activate, destroy and repair

ACTIVATION

A Specialist in Silhouette contact spends the Activate Antenna Short Skill and passes a Normal WIP roll. Failure can be retried by spending another Short Skill. Activation can be taken from the opponent. A destroyed Activated Antenna retains its activation. To activate a destroyed node, a Hacker must be wholly within that Zone of Influence and pass a Normal WIP-3 roll using the destroyed-node Short Skill.

PROFILE AND DEFENSE

ARM 5 / BTS 5 / STR 3 / S3; GizmoKit PH9. Destroy through Anti-materiel CC attacks or placed D-Charges, then remove the model. The ADS opposes every CC attack with an automatic roll of 8; no positive attacker CC MODs. A successful ADS roll inflicts a Stun hit, BTS save PS5; Immunity (Enhanced) and Immunity (BTS) do not help. Antennas may receive Engineer or GizmoKit repairs. Use the official sheet for full timing and profiles.

Access, specialists and game end

PLAYABLE TERRAIN

Solid walls, cabinets, masonry planters and cargo give physical cover; decorative foliage and light lines do not. Window and door openings are real. Rear parapet terraces are playable; pitched tile slopes are scenery-only. Darkness, bath water, sky cars and exhaust add no terrain or visibility rules. State 1 exposes the lowest floor, then successive floors; final state restores roofs. Changing floor views rebuilds the projected guides.

SPECIALISTS / END

Specialists: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Chain of Command and Specialist Operative. Repeaters and Servants cannot perform the reserved tasks for Hackers, Doctors or Engineers. Standard end: after Round 3. If a player begins their Active Turn in Retreat!, end after that turn. Killed includes Dead, Null at game end, and troopers never deployed as a model/marker. Agree all terrain before deployment.

Stage workflow and night effects

DEPLOY / CLEAR

Spawn the SET_ bag from the main Saved Objects folder and drop it on the Stage's DROP BAGS HERE area. There is no deployment button on the bag. Use the Stage's CLEAR TABLE control to remove the map, objectives, lights and sky traffic. Clear the previous map first. The full-table save includes Lobo's table and Stage. Workshop and Portal publication are separate.

VIEWS / LIGHTING

Night is the default. Baths and market lanterns are warm; garage and transit lights are cool. Wet patches have restrained sheen; most paving stays matte. Drainage and wall utilities add no new terrain rules. Four billboards cycle artwork. Sky traffic hides five stationary flight-pose cars, brighter following spot headlights and 9.5-inch tapered contrails. Floor views and Full rooftops control interiors. Mission guides show the 8-inch Exclusion strip and the three 120 mm influence circles. Guide, sky, neon, floor and reference controls remain available.

Hardlock.text:
HARDLOCK

IRONVEIL COMPLEX  /  300 POINTS  /  ITS 18

Scoring and game length

MAIN OBJECTIVES

At each Game Round's end: control the Enemy Beacon for 1 OP (up to 3 OP across three rounds).

At game end:
1 OP - Your Beacon is not enemy-controlled.
2 OP - You have more Activated Consoles.
1 OP per Activated Console (up to 3 OP).

CLASSIFIED, OVERVIEW AND ENDING

Each player has 1 Classified Objective, worth 1 OP. Maximum score: 10 OP.

Reinforcements are supported. Each player uses one HVT. Retreat! applies.

Play ends after Game Round 3. If a player starts an Active Turn in Retreat!, the game instead ends when that turn finishes.

Setup and deployment

300-POINT TABLE

Play area: 48 x 48 inches. Deploy from opposite X edges in zones 12 inches deep.

Side A (blue): X=-24 to -12.
Side B (orange): X=+12 to +24.

Deployment in Silhouette contact with a Beacon or Console is forbidden.

The overlay draws the forward boundaries only. Hardlock has no exclusion zone.

OBJECTIVE POSITIONS

Three Consoles on the centreline: (0,-12), (0,0), (0,+12), written as (X,Z). Use 40 mm Console tokens or scenery.

Two Beacons: (-12,0) and (+12,0), centred on each deployment front.

Your Enemy Beacon is the one at the enemy deployment front. Your supplied Panoply models represent the Beacons; Panoply rules do not apply.

Console activation and Specialists

ACTIVATE CONSOLE

Short Skill. Labels: Attack, Scenario.

A Specialist must be in Silhouette contact with a Console. Make a Normal WIP Roll.

After failure, another Short Skill allows another attempt.

Success activates the Console for your player, replacing any opposing ownership. Mark it with your distinct Player A/B Token.

SPECIALIST TROOPS

Eligible troops: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Chain of Command and Specialist Operative.

Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) models to carry out tasks restricted to Specialists.

Operational Learning for repeated failed Scenario Skills is on the Reference tab.

Controlling and picking up Beacons

CONTROL AN ENEMY BEACON

You control an Enemy Beacon while at least one of your non-Null Models is in Silhouette contact with it and no opposing non-Null trooper touches it.

Marker-state troopers cannot establish control.

Check control at the end of each Game Round for scoring. The separate end-game objective protects your own Beacon.

PICK UP BEACON

Short Skill. Labels: Attack, Scenario. No roll.

You must already have an Activated Console. The trooper must touch either:

- An Enemy Beacon with no opposing non-Null trooper touching it; or
- A friendly Normal-state trooper carrying an Enemy Beacon.

Spend the Short Skill to pick up or transfer the Beacon.

Carrying, dropping and model handling

CARRYING LIMITS

A Model normally carries at most one Beacon. Baggage allows up to two.

Marker states, including Camouflage, Impersonation and Holoechoes, cannot carry Beacons.

Keep a carried Beacon on the table and in Silhouette contact with its carrier.

DROPPING AND SCENERY

A carrier in, or entering, any Null State drops the Beacon. Place it just clear of Silhouette contact with that trooper.

Beacons never obstruct movement or Line of Fire.

The supplied Panoply pieces are movable Beacon models here. They do not add Panoply objectives, equipment rolls or Panoply Chart rules.

Operational Learning and other point levels

OPERATIONAL LEARNING

A Specialist repeating a failed Scenario Skill against the same target in consecutive Orders gains +3 WIP on Order 2; from Order 3, also gain +1SD. Other applicable Scenario MODs combine.

Success, changing skill or target, or ordering another trooper resets the sequence. Only one sequence per Scenario Skill may apply to a trooper.

OTHER POINT LEVELS

300 / 350 / 400: 48 x 48 table; 12-inch DZs; outer Consoles 12 inches from side edges.

200 / 250: 32 x 48 table; 12-inch DZs; outer Consoles 8 inches from side edges.

150: 24 x 32 table; 8-inch DZs; outer Consoles 6 inches from side edges.

This map stays the 48 x 48 setup; the overlay does not resize it.

Mission Geist: infinitygeist.com/mission/s18_hard_lock  |  ITS 18  |  Tabs are personal.

Last Launch.text:
LAST LAUNCH  -  PORT MERIDIAN

The Evening Star is making its final departure.

Play the current official Last Launch scenario. The centre pavilion is the 8 x 8 in Launching Tower, with four open Wide Gates and infinitely high walls for LoF. Its roof is not playable.

Two 40 mm ID Scanners sit on the centre line, 8 in from each flank edge. The 40 mm ID Checker is at the pavilion centre. Keep silhouette contact clear.

The shuttle is scenery. Extraction uses the ID Checker.

Standard deployment is 12 in from opposing X edges. Quadrants and exclusion markings are optional references; they add no scenario rules.

Akial Interference.text:
AKIAL INTERFERENCE

SWITCHBACK QUARTER / 300 POINTS / ITS 18

Akial Interference

SCORING

Common Classifieds: 1 OP each, maximum 6.

More accomplished Classifieds: 1 OP.

Accomplish a Classified every round: 1 OP, even if later canceled.

PRIVATE OBJECTIVE

Private Classified: 2 OP; immune to interference.

Deployment and objectives

300 POINTS

48 x 48 inches; opposite 12-inch deployment zones.

One central 40 mm antenna.

HVTs

Four HVTs per player; remove each after one completed objective.

No deployment touching antenna/HVTs. No Secure HVT/Treasure.

Classified cards

EACH ROUND

Two shared Common Classifieds: each player draws two, chooses one. Round one: retain the other privately; later rounds: discard it.

TRACKING

Retain accomplished cards; discard unaccomplished ones between rounds.

Duplicate names: first player reveals an extra card.

Use distinct targets/troopers for duplicates.

Antenna actions

EMIT INTERFERENCE

Specialist contact; Normal WIP. Retry failures. Once/specialist/round; once/eligible accomplished Common card.

Cancel an opponent accomplishment sharing its eligible symbol.

FILTER SIGNAL

Specialist contact; no roll. Replace a current Common card; archive it if accomplished, otherwise discard.

Specialists and game end

SPECIALISTS

Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Chain of Command, Specialist Operatives.

No remote Repeaters/Servants.

GAME END

Three rounds; Retreat! ends the game after that Active Turn.

This is a quick reference. Consult the official mission for full procedures and symbol eligibility.

Switchback Quarter

BUILDINGS

State 1 is the ground floor. Higher numbered states reveal upper floors, then the roof.

Use the stairs and ladders to reach upper levels. Furniture and murals are part of the building; signs leave openings clear.

TABLE

One central Akial antenna replaces the four old consoles. No quadrant scoring.

Use Deployment for Base, +4 or +8-inch front-line references. These references do not change the mission deployment size.

Each player brings four HVTs and their Classified Deck.

Quick reference. Official mission: experience.corvusbelli.com / ITS / Akial Interference

The Dig.text:
THE DIG

OLD QUARTER EXCAVATION / ITS18 / 48 x 48

Scoring and mission overview

OBJECTIVE POINTS

* Neutralize an already-analysed Hyperthermal Tech: 2 OP per Tech, up to three Techs / 6 OP.
* At game end, if you neutralized at least one Tech in every Game Round: 1 OP.
* At game end, if more Consoles carry your Player Token than the opponent's: 1 OP.
* Two Classified Objectives: 1 OP each.

OVERVIEW

Reinforcements-compatible. Retreat! applies. Each player uses one HVT and two Classified Objectives. Each completed Classified is worth 1 OP.

The task previously called Activate Console is Analyze Hyperthermal Tech. Console ownership and neutralization use Player Tokens; neutralization requires a Tech analysed for your own player. The small-game spacing exception applies at 150 points.

Corner deployment and consoles

DEPLOYMENT AND OBJECTIVES

This is the 48 x 48 inch, 300-point setup. Players deploy in opposite corner zones, each measured as a 24-inch radius from its corner. Neither player may deploy a trooper in Silhouette contact with a Console or Hyperthermal Tech.

There are three Consoles on the other diagonal: one at table centre, and one 16 inches in each direction from centre. Use Console A tokens or 40 mm diameter objective scenery. The familiar consoles supplied with this map have 40 mm mission footprints.

DEPLOYMENT AIDS

The Deployment menu can show 24-, 28- and 32-inch corner arcs independently. Side A (blue) and Side B (orange) can be selected separately, together, or hidden. The 24-inch arcs define the actual Deployment Zones. The 28-/32-inch arcs are +4-/+8-inch measuring aids; displaying them does not enlarge the mission's Deployment Zones or change Tech-placement restrictions. Apply the relevant troop's deployment rules normally.

* 300 / 350 / 400 points: 48 x 48 table; 24-inch corner zones.
* 200 / 250 points: 32 x 48 table; 20-inch corner zones.
* 150 points: 24 x 32 table; 12-inch corner zones; 4-inch Tech spacing.
This terrain remains the 48 x 48 setup; overlay selections do not resize it.

Place Hyperthermal Tech before deployment

PLACEMENT

Each player places three Hyperthermal Tech tokens. The player who kept Deployment places their three first.

Use 25 mm diameter Tech tokens or equivalent scenery. The WHOLE token must be more than 8 inches from BOTH players' Deployment Zones and from every other Tech token. It must be on accessible table ground, never on top of or inside scenery or a building. In a 150-point game these two spacing requirements are 4 inches instead.

Use the normal Infinity mod Hyperthermal Tech markers for player placement; this map creates no Tech models. Players choose positions that satisfy the restrictions above.

TERRAIN AND ACCESS

Use the modeled geometry for line of fire and cover. The three open excavation pockets are 2.5 inches below street level and are 8 by 7 inches with two staggered ramps apiece; there is no tunnel network. Buildings have usable interiors and roofs. Taller buildings: state 1 roof on, state 2 upper floor exposed, state 3 ground floor exposed. Single-storey buildings: state 1 roof on, state 2 ground floor exposed. External roof ladders persist in all states. Rubble has no automatic special terrain effect.

Analyze Hyperthermal Tech

DECLARE AND RESOLVE

Short Skill. Labels: Attack, Scenario.

Who and where:
* A Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with a Console that does not already have that player's own Player Token.

Resolution:
* Make a Normal WIP Roll. After failure, another attempt is allowed by spending another Short Skill.
* On success, remove the opponent's Player Token beside that Console and mark it for the active player.
* If the active player's total of analysed or neutralized Tech is still below three, the opponent chooses ANY currently unanalysed Tech token on the board to become analysed for the active player.
* Use distinguishable Player A/B tokens to show which player owns the Console and the analysed Tech. The choice of Tech belongs to the opponent, not to the Specialist's owner.

SPECIALIST TROOPS

For this mission: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, and troops with Chain of Command or Specialist Operative.

Repeaters and Peripheral (Servant) models cannot be used by Hackers, Doctors or Engineers to carry out tasks that require a Specialist Troop.

Neutralize Tech and build momentum

NEUTRALIZE HYPERTHERMAL TECH

Short Skill. Labels: Attack, Scenario.

Any trooper may perform this task, provided it is in Silhouette contact with an analysed Tech bearing its OWN player's token. No roll is required. Remove that Tech token from the table after neutralization.

OPERATIONAL LEARNING

After a Specialist fails a WIP Roll for a Scenario-labelled Skill, continuing the SAME task in consecutive Orders gives:
* Second consecutive Order: +3 WIP.
* Third consecutive Order and later consecutive Orders: +3 WIP and +1SD.
These bonuses combine with other applicable Scenario-skill MODs.

The same Specialist must keep using the same Scenario Skill against the same target, without interruption. A successful roll, using a different Skill, changing target, or spending an Order on another trooper resets the sequence. Only one sequence may apply to a trooper for a given Scenario Skill at a time.

Final checks and game length

END CONDITIONS

Play ends after the third Game Round. If a player begins their Active Turn in Retreat!, the game finishes at the end of that turn.

Record whether at least one Tech was neutralized in each Game Round before final scoring. Count Console ownership, neutralized Tech and Classified Objectives.

REFERENCE AND REMINDERS

Analyze removes the opponent's Console token. When a Tech is analysed, the opponent selects the currently unanalysed Tech for the active player.

Neutralize needs a Tech bearing your own Player Token.

Annihilation.text:
ANNIHILATION

CANOPY BLACKSITE / 300 POINTS / ITS 18

Annihilation | 300 points

ENEMY CASUALTIES

Score 1 OP for 75-150 enemy Army Points killed, 3 OP for 151-250, or 4 OP for more than 250. Use only the highest applicable band.

SURVIVAL AND LIEUTENANT

Score 1 OP for 75-150 surviving VP, 3 OP for 151-250, or 4 OP for more than 250. Killing the enemy Lieutenant earns 2 OP. Maximum total: 10 OP.

Forces and deployment

TABLE AND DEPLOYMENT

300 points / 6 SWC. Table: 48 x 48 inches. Opposite deployment zones are 12 inches deep along the X edges; fronts are X=-12 and X=+12.

MISSION ELEMENTS

No HVT, Secure HVT or Classified Deck is used. No exclusion zone or mission objective pieces are required.

Casualties

WHAT COUNTS

Enemy troops in Dead State, or a Null State at game end, count as killed. Troops never deployed as a model or marker also count as killed by the opponent.

SCORING RECORD

Record the points killed, your surviving Victory Points, and whether you killed the enemy Lieutenant.

Game length

NO QUARTER

Retreat! does not apply in this mission.

END OF THE GAME

The mission ends after the third Game Round. Calculate casualty, survival and Lieutenant points then.

Canopy Blacksite terrain

SOLID COVER AND WINDOWS

Use actual model geometry for line of fire, cover and movement. Roof states expose real interiors. Exterior access remains available.

JUNGLE VISIBILITY

Trees toggle between leaf-on and leaf-off states. Agree how foliage is treated before play; toggling it for access does not alter your agreed terrain treatment.

Map controls

RIGHT-SIDE DRAWER

Map Controls starts open. Deployment toggles the two thin fronts. Mission opens this six-tab reference. Day / Night / Background Off changes the environment.

CLEAR TABLE

Use the stage Clear Table control before loading another map. Changed building and tree states retain map tags for cleanup. Grid and snapping start off.

Official Corvus Belli Annihilation reference, checked 1 Nov 2026.

Superiority.text:
SUPERIORITY

FROSTLINE RELAY  /  300 POINTS  /  ITS 18

Superiority scoring

EACH GAME ROUND

At the end of each of the three Game Rounds, dominate more midfield Quadrants than your opponent to score 2 OP.

Equal numbers of dominated Quadrants score neither player these points.

Round scoring can provide up to 6 OP.

END OF THE GAME

Score 1 OP for each Console your side has successfully Hacked, up to 4 OP across the four Consoles.

Both players can score the same Console if both have Hacked it.

The scenario provides a maximum of 10 OP per player.

Table and objective setup

300 POINTS | 48 x 48 INCHES

Deployment zones are 12 inches deep on opposite X edges. Their front lines are X=-12 and X=+12.

Four 40 mm Consoles are centred at:
(-6,-12), (+6,-12), (-6,+12), (+6,+12).

Coordinates are X,Z in inches, relative to table centre.

ZONES AND MARKINGS

The four midfield Quadrants lie between the deployment fronts. X=0 and Z=0 divide that region into four equal zones, each 12 x 24 inches.

Deployment toggles only the two thin front lines. Quadrants has its own optional overlay.

This mission has no exclusion zone. HVTs and the Classified Deck are not used.

Dominating Quadrants

WHICH TROOPS COUNT

Compare the Victory Points of eligible troops in each zone. The player with the greater total dominates it.

More than half a troop base must be inside that zone.

Models, genuine troop Markers, Proxies and Peripheral Troops can count. Null troops ordinarily do not count.

EXCEPTIONS AND EXCLUSIONS

Shasvastii troops count in the Unconscious state or a non-Null state.

A non-Null troop with Baggage contributes an extra 20 VP toward domination.

Mines, Deployable Repeaters, other equipment tokens and fake Holoechoes do not count.

Check domination at the end of each Game Round.

Hack Consoles

SHORT SKILL | ATTACK, SCENARIO

An eligible Specialist Troop must be in Silhouette contact with the Console.

Make a Normal WIP Roll. Success records that Console as Hacked by your side.

Failure can be retried by spending another corresponding Short Skill and making another roll. Operational Learning may apply.

BOTH SIDES CAN HACK

The other player can Hack a previously Hacked Console using the same procedure. Both players then retain credit for that Console.

Use two different player-token types, and retain both when both sides succeed.

Console scoring is checked at game end; it is not exclusive ownership.

Specialists and Operational Learning

ELIGIBLE SPECIALISTS

Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Chain of Command troops and Specialist Operatives qualify.

Hackers, Doctors and Engineers cannot use Repeaters or Peripheral (Servant) models to perform the required specialist task.

The acting Specialist must satisfy the Console contact requirement.

CONSECUTIVE FAILED ATTEMPTS

After a failed Scenario-labelled WIP task, the same troop retrying the same Skill against the same target in the next Order receives +3 WIP.

In the third consecutive Order and later: +3 WIP and +1SD. These combine with other applicable MODs.

Success, another Skill or target, or an Order spent on another troop resets the sequence. Only one sequence per troop and Scenario Skill applies.

Game end and scorekeeping

WHEN THE GAME ENDS

The mission normally ends after the third Game Round.

If a player starts their Active Turn in Retreat!, it ends at the end of that Turn.

Record Quadrant points after each completed Game Round, then calculate the Hacked Console points when the game ends.

QUICK CHECKLIST

Track the four Consoles separately for each player. Both sides can have credit for one Console.

No HVT Model, Secure HVT or Classified Deck is used.

The map is set for 300 points. Consult the official mission for other table sizes.

Reference: official ITS18, version 2026.09.11, pages 135-138.

Frontline.text:
FRONTLINE

AURORA VII / LEGACY ITS16 / 48 x 48 / Greenwood River Crossing

Scoring and timing

SECTORS AT GAME END

Dominate your nearest sector: 1 OP.

Dominate the middle sector: 2 OP.

Dominate the farthest sector: 3 OP.

Sector objectives are assessed at the end of the game, not each round.

CLASSIFIED OBJECTIVES

Four Classified Objectives per player, worth 1 OP each. Maximum total: 10 OP.

The first Classified card can instead be committed to INTELCOM Support and Control before play; see INTELCOM.

Deployment and board setup

DEPLOYMENT

This map uses a 48 x 48 inch table, with opposing 12 x 48 inch Deployment Zones along X = -24 and +24. The forward boundaries are X = -12 and +12. The thin overlay marks those fronts only; it grants no additional deployment permissions.

No mission Exclusion Zone is specified. Frontline does not use consoles. Tactical Support Options: 0.

CAMPAIGN SETUP

Keep the chosen territory rules, owner advantage and current Campaign Event in effect for a territory game. Check the current Turn briefing before play. The mission stays Frontline/Supremacy; these archive missions are not renamed to an ITS18 scenario.

Use the supplied terrain layout. Agree terrain boundaries and any Campaign Event changes before deployment. QAZ templates are placed by the players, as described on the QAZ tab.

The three scoring sectors

EXACT AREAS

All three sectors span the full 48-inch width along Z.

X = -12 to -4: nearest for the player deploying at X = -24.

X = -4 to +4: central sector.

X = +4 to +12: nearest for the player deploying at X = +24.

DOMINATION

A sector or quadrant belongs to the player with the greater total of eligible Victory Points inside it. A tie gives neither player domination. More than half a trooper's base must lie inside the area.

Models and genuine trooper Markers count, including eligible Proxies and Peripherals. Null troopers, fake Holoechoes, Mines, Deployable Repeaters and other equipment tokens do not count. Shasvastii also count in Shasvastii-Embryo State.

Eligible non-Null Baggage adds 20 VP to the area occupied. Deployment Zones lie outside these scoring sectors.

INTELCOM and Classified cards

COMMIT BEFORE PLAY

After choosing the first Classified card, declare whether it will be used as a Classified Objective or as INTELCOM Support and Control. Both players roll a die; the higher result announces this choice first.

The card text and numeric value remain private.

SUPPORT AND CONTROL

At final scoring, resolve INTELCOM in Initiative order. Add the committed card's number to your VP in one chosen sector.

You must have at least one non-Null trooper in that sector. A card committed to INTELCOM is not also a scored Classified Objective.

Quantum Anomaly Zones

PLACE BEFORE DEPLOYMENT

Each player places one Circular Template, on a surface at least as large as the template. It must be wholly outside both Deployment Zones and cannot overlap another QAZ.

The player who kept Deployment places first.

EFFECTS

The template is Difficult Terrain (Zero-G) and a Saturation Zone.

An active trooper declaring or performing an Order inside it makes a BTS Saving Roll against PS 10; failure loses one Wound/Structure point.

Apply any explicit Campaign Event replacement or exception.

End-of-game checklist

END AND SCORE

The mission lasts three Game Rounds. The Frontline sheet specifies no early ending when a player enters Retreat!; apply the normal Retreat! rules.

Resolve INTELCOM, count VP in each sector and award 1 / 2 / 3 OP from each player's perspective. Add completed Classifieds.

REPORT THE RESULT

Record both OP totals and surviving VP. Submit one campaign result for both players and have the opponent confirm it. Territory-game Tournament Points remain part of the territory totals.

Use the written Turn briefing for the current reporting deadline and campaign rewards.

Corvus Belli ITS16 Part II v1.0.2, pp. 37-38; campaign Turn briefing overrides where stated.

Supremacy.text:
SUPREMACY

AURORA VII / LEGACY ITS16 / 48 x 48 / Greenwood River Crossing

Round scoring and final objectives

AT EACH ROUND END

Dominate more quadrants than the opponent: 2 OP.

Dominate the same number: 1 OP each, only if each player dominates at least one quadrant.

No dominated quadrants means no tie point. Score this after each of three rounds.

AT GAME END

Each console you have hacked: 1 OP, maximum 3 OP.

One Classified Objective per player: 1 OP.

Maximum normal score: 10 OP. The specified INTELCOM Provisions symbol can add 1 OP to its Classified if the player remains below 10 OP.

Deployment, quadrants and consoles

DEPLOYMENT

This map uses a 48 x 48 inch table, with opposing 12 x 48 inch Deployment Zones along X = -24 and +24. The forward boundaries are X = -12 and +12. The thin overlay marks those fronts only; it grants no additional deployment permissions.

No mission Exclusion Zone is specified. Tactical Support Options: 0.

SCORING AREAS AND CONSOLES

The central area outside both Deployment Zones is divided at X = 0 and Z = 0 into four 12 x 24 inch quadrants.

Console centers: X = +/-6, Z = +/-12. Use the provided 40 mm consoles; models may stand on terrain while retaining the required horizontal positions.

Keep the chosen territory rules, owner advantage and current Campaign Event in effect for a territory game. Check the current Turn briefing before play. The mission stays Frontline/Supremacy; these archive missions are not renamed to an ITS18 scenario.

Hacking consoles and Specialist Troops

HACK CONSOLE

Short Skill with Attack and Scenario labels. A Specialist must be in Silhouette contact with the console and pass a Normal WIP Roll. A failed attempt may be repeated with another Short Skill.

Both players can hack the same console; one player's success does not erase the other's success. Track each player separately.

SPECIALISTS AND HACKERS

Eligible Specialists: Hackers, Doctors, Engineers, Forward Observers, Paramedics, Chain of Command and Specialist Operative.

Repeaters and Servant Peripherals cannot perform a Specialist's task for them.

Hackers receive +3 WIP and may make two WIP Rolls for each Short Skill spent hacking a console.

Which troopers count

AREA CONTROL

A sector or quadrant belongs to the player with the greater total of eligible Victory Points inside it. A tie gives neither player domination. More than half a trooper's base must lie inside the area.

Measure only the four central quadrants. Troopers in the Deployment Zones do not contribute to them.

ELIGIBLE POINTS

Models and genuine trooper Markers count, including eligible Proxies and Peripherals. Null troopers, fake Holoechoes, Mines, Deployable Repeaters and other equipment tokens do not count. Shasvastii also count in Shasvastii-Embryo State.

An eligible non-Null Baggage trooper adds 20 VP to its quadrant. Count and award round OP only at the end of each Game Round.

QAZ Creatures

PLACE BEFORE DEPLOYMENT

Each player places one stationary QAZ Creature at least 8 inches outside the enemy Deployment Zone. The player who kept Deployment places first.

Use a Player Token or Silhouette 1 model. It is a Deployable Weapon, not a mobile trooper.

PROFILE AND REACTIONS

CC 11 | ARM 1 | BTS 3 | VITA 1 | S1. AP CC Weapon; CC Attack Burst 3 in ARO; Guard without LoF.

It reacts with CC Attack to an Order declared or performed by an active enemy Model, not a Marker, within ZoC. A blocked or impassable Guard path makes the attack Idle. Remove it after losing its VITA. Apply explicit Campaign Event exceptions.

Game length and result

END CONDITIONS

End after Game Round 3. If a player starts their Active Turn in Retreat!, end the game at the end of that Turn.

Count final hacked consoles for each player, up to 3 OP, then Classifieds and applicable Provisions. Keep round OP already scored.

CAMPAIGN REPORT

Record OP, surviving VP and the territory played. Submit one result for both players, then confirm it. Territory-game Tournament Points count toward territory totals.

The current Turn briefing determines available territories, the Event and campaign rewards.
